pass_means: SELF-CHECK = internal consistency only: identities, convergence and agreement with our own closed forms.  It says NOTHING about agreement with the publication; that is the 'verdict' column of the summary table in docs/validation/published_benchmarks.md, and several rows there disagree while the self-check passes.

rows.source: from 3 mm NbTi at 330 A filling the winding cross-section
rescaled to the published 5 T peak

magnet.note: Uniform current density over the published winding envelope; the 9-fold axial segmentation and the 3 soft-iron flux-return segments are not modelled (their positions are not published).

pickup.note: The CORE template is a superconducting toroidal cavity around the solenoid, read out across a neck gap in its inner wall.  DMRadio-Core's pickup instead closes across the bore with two copper plates (6 cm apart) and is read out through a 30-degree azimuthal sector of the slit; neither the copper plates nor the fractional port are axisymmetric, so these numbers are a model of the topology, not of the device.  CORE publishes no L_eff or |V| to compare with.

scan_time.note: eta_A is the published dc-SQUID optimum (arXiv:2504.20398 Fig. 3; 8.1 at 70 MHz to 11.7 at 140 MHz), log-averaged over the band; eta_A = 1 (the SQL) is kept as a floor for reference.  These scan times use the MQS Psi and L_p, which at 70-140 MHz are only the omega -> 0 limit: the beyond-MQS values are in the `fullwave` record and are much larger (section 6).

pass_scope: the magnet stored energy within 10 % of the published 4.3 MJ on the published envelope (a genuine agreement), and that the pickup variants solved.  It does NOT test the Core scan time, which disagrees by 4-11x.
headline: magnet at 5 T peak: W = 4.43 MJ vs published 4.3 MJ (+3.0 %); pickup model: 2/2 solved
